childrenite.identity: IMA G1823, Fe2+Al(PO4)(OH)2(H2O); distinct from Mn-dominant eosphorite. Natural Homolka grains; no microbial or inherited criticality assertion.
childrenite.inspected: Full main10pages/Figures1–6/Tables1–3; official3-memberSI including all20workbook spots and CIF structural/atomic fields.
childrenite.claims: Two grains collected11July2020 from two outcrops. Twenty spots across these two grains, not twenty specimens. Fe/(Fe+Mn)0.51–0.86. GrainA single-crystal refinement Cmca,602observedreflections,R1=.0295 and Raman/bond-valence interpretation. Methods3.1–3.5; Table1p4; Tables2–3p5; Figures2–3p6,4p7,5–6p8.
limits: Older Handbook Bba2/possible monoclinic assignment is distinguished from this Cmca specimen.
Main Table2 temperature293(2)K and5682measuredreflections conflict with CIF273(2)K and5429.
CIF Fe/Ca scattering/formula-sum fields are not interpreted as measured Fe/Mn/Ca chemistry; analyticalSi0.04 differs from approximatelySi0.01 in main formula.
TotalFe reported asFeO, water calculated bycharge balance; totals>100% interpreted byauthors asbeam dehydration, not controlled transformation.
Probable uraninite inclusions are not independently phase-confirmed. No organism, formation experiment, yield or extraction assay.
Raman glue features and missing water-bending peak constrain interpretation; divalent bond-valence inference is not direct Fe-valence measurement of every grain.
childrenite.lineage: Main, CIF and workbook are one study. Figure4 includes six prior Nahodilova2022 points as comparison, not additional2024 sampled grains.

hureaulite.identity: IMA Rn2007s.p.; Mn2+5(PO3OH)2(PO4)2(H2O)4. Natural mineral identity kept separate from source-assigned synthetic C2/c reagent-derived powder.
hureaulite.inspected: Full18-page main/Figures1–8/Table1 and official11-pageSI/FiguresS1–S13/all model equations.
hureaulite.claims: Abiotic5wt%SDS/MnCl2·4H2O synthesis, SDS/Mn1.8,70C1h then Mn/K2HPO4=1,70C24h; water/acetone washed,room-temperature dried. MainFigures1–2 support source phase/morphology assignment; BET4m2/g and approximate40nm thickness, not particle-size distribution. Composite70:20:10powder/carbon/PTFE,7mgactive/cm2,three-electrode184F/g at5mV/s in3MKOH versus16/15F/g in neutral electrolytes; about100F/g at100mV/s. Separate two-electrode Swagelok5MKOH cell and cycling loss, no complete-device energy claim.
limits: No absolute synthesis quantities/volume,pH,yield,SDS-freecontrol or independent phase-fraction/purity determination.
Table1K3PO4=1M conflicts with methods/plots3M; no resolution inferred.
Equations2–3 labelWh/kg andtime seconds without explicit time-unit conversion. Exactenergy/power/Ragone superiority not adopted.
SI specific-surface-area units conflict between active-depth and areal definitions; S13two-electrode caption versus Ag/AgCl axis remains unresolved.
Dunn/Trasatti fitted partitions and assumed one-electron depth are models, not direct ionic or Mn-valence identification. Proposed Grotthuss/Mnredox is not proven.
No electrode-blank subtraction, independentreplicate uncertainty, postcyclingphase analysis or dissolvedMn mass balance; activepowder capacitance denominator is notdeviceenergy or metalrecovery.
hureaulite.lineage: All main/SI measurements belong to one2024study; no independent replication inferred. Earlier2012/2020 sources were not fully acquired and their claims were not imported.
